agencies.painsTitle: What an agency stops doing by hand

1.title: New business between deliveries
1.body: Prospecting is the first thing to slip when a project runs late. A Coworker keeps building the list and writing to it, calm week or not.

2.title: The same report, times twelve
2.body: Numbers pulled, commented and sent, one per account, every month. The work is identical each time, so a Coworker does it on schedule.

3.title: Invoices nobody dares chase
3.body: The reminder due on day 31 goes out on day 60. A Coworker sends it on day 31, in your words, and lists who still owes you.

features.workspaces: A Box per client with access per person, or a workspace of its own for a hard wall.
features.second-brain: Each client’s tone, offer and rules, read before any Coworker writes.
features.coworkers-work-together: One audits the site, the next writes the brief, a third drafts the posts.
features.human-in-the-loop: A budget move or a client email waits for your yes when you want it to.

1.question: Can I keep each client separate?
1.answer: Yes. Put each client in a Box: it is free, and you pick who on the team reaches it. Boxes share one machine and one database, so for a hard wall, give a client its own workspace, with its own apps, Brain and plan.

2.question: Will the work sound like us, or like a robot?
2.answer: Your tone, your offer and your rules live in the Brain, and every Coworker reads them before it writes. On a client’s workspace, that is the client’s tone. Correct a Coworker once and it remembers the correction.

3.question: Do we pay per seat or per client?
3.answer: Seats are free and unlimited on Pro, so the whole team, and the client if you want, can read the work and answer an approval. Boxes are free too. Only a separate workspace comes with a plan of its own.

4.question: Can it work in our clients’ ad accounts?
4.answer: It reviews Google, Meta, LinkedIn and TikTok ads, flags wasted spend and proposes budget moves, exclusions and the next creatives to test. You decide in its instructions what it may change and what comes to you first.

1.question: Is this worth it for one person?
1.answer: That is the case it was built for: the jobs you would hire for if hiring made sense. One plan runs as many Coworkers as you build, with no fee per run or per task.

2.question: Does it work while my laptop is shut?
2.answer: Yes. Your Coworkers run on a machine of your own in the cloud, in Europe. The Monday run happens whether you are at your desk, with a client or on holiday.

3.question: Can it send things in my name without asking?
3.answer: Only as far as you let it. You decide in its instructions whether it sends or hands you a draft, and it brings anything consequential to you as an approval first.

4.question: Does prospecting on LinkedIn cost extra?
4.answer: Yes. LinkedIn Pro is a paid app: {linkedinPrice} a month per connected account, on the same invoice as your plan. Your Coworkers then message and follow up from your account, at a recommended daily pace that keeps it safe.

5.question: Will it file my taxes?
5.answer: No. It prepares your VAT returns and tax files from your books, with the source behind every figure, ready for you or your accountant to check and submit.

3.body: The messaging, the landing page, the emails, the post. A Coworker drafts the lot from the spec while you build.

1.question: How long before a Coworker is useful?
1.answer: Minutes, if you start from a template: you connect its apps, check its schedule and it runs. Building one from your own description takes about as long as writing the job down.

2.question: Can the whole team use it?
2.answer: Yes, and it costs nothing extra: seats are free and unlimited on Pro. Everyone sees the same board, can give a Coworker work and can answer when one asks for a yes.

3.question: Does it replace our automation tools?
3.answer: It replaces the ones you keep fixing. A Coworker is told the job, not drawn as a flow, so a new field or a renamed column does not break it the way a node graph does.

4.question: Where do the prospects’ emails come from?
4.answer: From your CRM and the web, and from lookups of work emails, phone numbers and company data. It is paid data, drawn from your Rerun credits, and the Coworker asks you to approve the estimated cost before it buys.

5.question: Does the bill grow with the team?
5.answer: No. Coworkers, seats and runs are unlimited on Pro. What costs extra is what you choose to use: paid data on your Rerun credits, and LinkedIn Pro or WhatsApp Pro per connected account.

1.question: Where does it read our usage and billing data from?
1.answer: From the tools you already use: Stripe, your database or warehouse, your product analytics, your support desk. You connect them once in the Vault and switch them on for the Coworkers that need them.

1.question: Does a Coworker give legal advice?
1.answer: No. It reads, extracts and flags, and every output is written for a qualified person to review. It says where in the document each point came from, so you can check it in seconds.

2.question: Where do our documents live?
2.answer: In your own drives and tools, which the Coworker reads with the access you give it. What it works on stays on your workspace’s machine in Europe, isolated from other customers and backed up each night, encrypted.

3.question: Who else sees our files?
3.answer: Your workspace runs on its own machine, apart from every other customer. The model you choose reads what a task needs, under that provider’s terms. Rerun is open source, so a firm that needs it can run it on its own servers.

4.question: Can we encode our own clause standards?
4.answer: Yes. Your positions, your red lines and your fallback wording go in the Brain or in a skill, and the Coworker reviews against them rather than against a generic checklist.

5.question: Can we keep matters apart?
5.answer: A Box per matter decides who on the team reaches its Coworkers. Boxes share one machine and one database, so a matter that needs a hard wall gets a workspace of its own.
